# Purpose

*A single, plain-language answer to the question "what data do we actually have?" — the complete inventory pulled from the EcoCommons production environment, summarised by category and collection, with a compact per-collection profile available to download.*

This page is the companion **data** to the [production catalogue audit](ecocommons_prod_data_audit.qmd), which explains *how* the list was extracted (via `POST /api/es/search/dataset`, paginated on `uuid`). Here we just show *what came back*.

::: callout-important
**Records are not products.** The headline count of **58,424** is a *layer-level* number — one variable, for one model, one scenario, one month is a single record. A single product, *WorldClim v2.1 future climate*, expands into **52,308 records (≈90% of the catalogue)**. For a "what do we have" view, the **collection-level** breakdown below is the meaningful one; the raw record count is dominated by that combinatorial expansion.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Download the summaries

The meaningful "what do we have" information is published here as two small, text-based files. The full 58,424-row record list and the grouped Excel workbook are *not* hosted on this site — they are large binaries and every number worth reporting is already rolled up below. They can be regenerated on demand with `extract_prod_datasets.py` (see the [audit](ecocommons_prod_data_audit.qmd)).

| File | Contents | Download |
|------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------|
| **Collection profiles** (`.csv`) | One row per collection — records, category, time domain, resolution(s), spatial domain, data type, year range, downloadability. The table in [By collection](#by-collection) below. | [collection_profiles.csv](data/collection_profiles.csv) |
| **Summary** (`.json`) | The aggregate category / time-domain / collection counts behind the charts on this page. | [prod_dataset_summary.json](data/prod_dataset_summary.json) |

Each underlying record carries these fields:

`title` · `uuid` · `data_category` · `data_subcategories` · `time_domain` · `year` · `resolution` · `spatial_domain` · `spatial_data_type` · `collection_names` · `downloadable` · `created`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# At a glance

| Measure | Value |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Dataset records (layers) | **58,424** |
| Distinct collections (products) | **54** (53 named + an orphan bucket) |
| Dominant product | WorldClim v2.1 future climate — **52,308** records (≈90%) |
| Future vs current | 54,614 future · 3,810 current |
| Uncategorised records | 45 (≈0.08%) |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# By category

The catalogue is overwhelmingly **climate** data — 95% of all records.

| Category | Records | Share |
|:--------------------------|---------:|------:|
| Climate | 55,485 | 95.0% |
| Vegetation | 2,099 | 3.6% |
| Biodiversity | 407 | 0.7% |
| Marine | 204 | 0.3% |
| Topography | 129 | 0.2% |
| Human Activity | 18 | 0.0% |
| Freshwater | 17 | 0.0% |
| Soil | 11 | 0.0% |
| Boundary Data | 9 | 0.0% |
| *(uncategorised / unknown)* | 45 | 0.08% |

The nine category values above are the controlled vocabulary adopted in [`MD-001`](rule_book.qmd#md-001) of the Rule Book; the 45 uncategorised records are exactly the ones that rule flags.

# By time domain

| Time domain | Records | Share |
|:------------|--------:|------:|
| Future | 54,614 | 93.5% |
| Current | 3,810 | 6.5% |

Every record carries a time domain — none are missing. `Historical` is defined in the vocabulary ([`MD-002`](rule_book.qmd#md-002)) but is currently unused in production.

The long tail matters for governance: **289 records sit in no collection** (the `None` orphan bucket), and many products exist as a single layer. These are exactly the datasets [`DS-002`](rule_book.qmd#ds-002) is designed to catch. The full download set (`downloadable: No`) is concentrated in **WorldClim-v2.1** and **eBird** — the two biggest products — which [`DS-004`](rule_book.qmd#ds-004) flags for an explicit access decision.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# How this connects to the Rule Book

This catalogue is the evidence base for the [Rule Book](rule_book.qmd): the category vocabulary, the time-domain values, the collection-membership checks, and the "Current status" figures in each rule all come from the numbers on this page. Re-pulling the catalogue and re-checking it against the rules is how we measure whether the platform's metadata quality is improving over time.
